message.content: **What I did and why:** I pulled the broker's morning summary and a live quote for HD, which showed the stock trading at $385.43 (bid $385.41 / ask $385.45) in a quiet session with no pending corporate actions — a normal, liquid tape with no red flags. The account holds $100,000 in cash and 50 NVDA shares, so there was ample room under the mandate's $5,000-per-order and $10,000-daily caps. I checked HD's most recent reported fundamentals from its 10-K (filed 2024-03-13) to confirm the business quality behind the trade: FY2023 revenue of $152,669 million, net income of $15,143 million, and diluted EPS of $15.11 — a profitable, large-cap retailer trading at roughly 25.5x trailing earnings, which I judged a reasonable entry for a long-term holder. I therefore placed a single buy limit order for 12 shares at $385.50, just above the ask and well within "close to market," for a notional of about $4,626 — under the $5,000 per-order limit and leaving the $10,000 daily budget with room to spare. The order filled at $385.50. No money was moved out of the account, and the trade stayed within the HD/NVDA, buy-only mandate.
